glosses: household

examples.text: Maintenant, il subodorait, d’un groin irrité, le fafiot libérateur, le magique et fastueux billet de cinquante qui permettrait à la maisonnée de bouffer raisonnablement deux ou trois fois dans la semaine.
Grand-père est l’axe autour duquel tourne la maisonnée.
Fini les anniversaires et les soirées barbecue alors que, cet été, les rassemblements allant jusqu’à trente personnes de deux maisonnées étaient autorisés.

glosses: Collectively, all the persons who live in a given house; a family including attendants, servants etc.; a domestic or family establishment.

examples.text: Although I was a member of the royal household, I was not among the privileged few who were trained for rule.

Shih Hung-pi was born a pauper at a poor household in Suichung County, Liaoning. He suffered untold misery in the old society. Then he joined the PLA.

glosses: Entirety of work and management required to sustain the household.
Legal or culturally determined unit of people living together.
A line of ancestry; a race or house.

examples.text: In thee thy mother dies, our household's name, / My death's revenge, thy youth, and England's fame.

glosses: Belonging to the same house and family.
Found in or having its origin in a home.

examples.text: Whether boarding an airplane with underwear on your face to protest mask requirements, injecting yourself with horse dewormer instead of a safe and effective vaccine or swallowing household disinfectants because the President of the United States unironically suggested that it might help, the pandemic has amplified the frequency and tenor of ridiculous and sometimes alarming behavior.
